sections.title: 1. What this doc is and how it was built
bullets: Second of 6 case-study docs (3a–3f, one per H2 9173 topic). Same format as 3a v1, which the user approved: facts table, 1 chart, what happened, how it fits, exam angle, 'Links' line, sources.

Topic 1.2 has 16 case-study slots taken from the syllabus content points. There are 18 cases, because two slots have pairs: states' influence over TNCs (strong vs limited) and labour unions (succeeded vs failed). 19 pages: slot plan, then one case per page.
This topic has the 'trend' and 'actors' types: three Trends slots (flows; towards manufacturing; towards services) and seven Actors slots (states, labour, ASEAN, WTO, World Bank).
Built straight to v1 (no preview), as the user said 'yes please' to starting 3b after approving 3a's format.
Built with tools/build_case_studies.py from tools/data/case_studies_3b.json; charts from tools/case_charts.py (1_2_*.png).

sections.title: 2. Assumptions
bullets: 'Varying degree of states' influence' is treated like a strategy slot, with a strong and a limited case (India/TikTok, Ireland/Apple).
One case per multilateral institution named in the syllabus (ASEAN, WTO, World Bank).
Cases reuse doc 3a where they fit: the WTO case is the Indonesia nickel ban from 3a slot 15; Links lines point across both docs.
Same limits as 3a: photo sites are blocked, so each image is a chart, timeline or number tiles; web pages could not be opened, so figures come from search results quoting each source.
A few lines give general background that is not in the listed sources (e.g. why carmakers ran short of chips; that Apple owns no assembly plants). They are widely reported but worth a check.
